The opportunity of our time

The people doing the work are already here. What’s missing is coherence.

Across the world, communities, Indigenous peoples, innovators and regenerative practitioners are already restoring forests, healing watersheds, protecting sacred sites, educating future generations and renewing local economies.

Most funding still flows in short cycles. Projects are funded, projects end, communities reapply, relationships reset and momentum is lost. The challenges we face are measured in generations, and they need structures built for generations.

Naluʻea is not another foundation or another fund. It is an ecosystem of perpetual entities designed so that resources compound rather than run dry: the base strengthens, knowledge accumulates, relationships deepen and the capacity to support living systems grows over time.

The name

Naluʻea comes from the Hawaiian for the amniotic fluid, the waters of becoming. It points toward birth and rebirth, and the renewal of flow in service of planetary regeneration.

Capital that behaves like water

In a watershed, water circulates, nourishes and returns. Held this way, capital doesn’t extract value from living systems. It participates in their flourishing, feeding the ecosystems and communities it touches and then flowing onward, renewed with each generation.

The system is built to outlast any single project, founder or funding cycle.

The flowing current

Living Treasury

Every contribution enters here. Principal is preserved and invested under a binding Investment Policy Statement, and the yield flows outward to the Living Nodes found ready. A gift given once keeps funding regeneration across generations.

Capital here is non-equity and non-governance: no contribution, at any scale, confers ownership or control.

The vault

Living Trust

Land and long-term assets are held apart from the cash endowment, insulated from the operational risk of active work. A perpetual, irrevocable trust established in Wyoming and Switzerland as of October 2025, held for the benefit of All Life.

What enters the Trust cannot be redirected by any future board, market, donor or crisis, for seven generations and beyond.

The Planetary Party Protocol

How readiness is cultivated

Capital flows best where a community is ready to receive it. The Planetary Party Protocol is how that readiness is cultivated.

Inspired by Barbara Marx Hubbard’s Wheel of Co-Creation, and recognizing that transformation requires all social functions working in harmony, the Planetary Party Protocol convenes the full spectrum of a bioregional community across all twelve domains: Arts & Culture, Economics, Education, Environment, Governance, Health, Infrastructure, Justice, Media, Relations, Science & Technology and Spirituality.

Within each bioregion, the Protocol unfolds through structured gatherings designed to map community stakeholders and existing regenerative initiatives, foster strategic connections and develop collective intelligence, form cross-sector working circles aligned on higher purpose, and create a marketplace of high-impact solutions with the financial mechanisms to fund them.

Like the tipping point described in complexity theory, small islands of coherence can shift larger systems when connected intentionally. The Planetary Party exists to identify, strengthen and connect these islands.

Flow Funds within each bioregion support early-stage initiatives, providing catalytic capital, enabling experimentation and building proof of concept. As initiatives mature, they interface with the larger Naluʻea capital architecture.

Emergence flows upward. Structure flows downward.

Our core principles

What holds every decision

These principles explain why the system is designed the way it is: why it stewards rather than extracts, listens before it acts, and measures its work by whether life flourishes.

  • Reverence for all life

    Life is a living whole to be honored, not a resource to be managed. Ecosystems, communities, cultures and future generations carry inherent worth beyond any assigned value.

  • Relationship before transaction

    We move at the speed of trust, entering communities as long-term partners. Capital arrives by invitation, not imposition, flowing toward communities that have signaled readiness.

  • Stewardship before ownership

    We seek to tend life, not own it. Capital serves mission; mission does not serve capital. No contribution, at any scale, acquires control over the purpose it supports.

  • Ancestral wisdom, living guidance

    Guided by the powers of nature and the custodians of Indigenous and modern technologies alike, we hold the past as a living partner and keep the spiritual technologies of our ancestors alive.

  • Future generations at the table

    Children and youth are emerging stewards, innovators, leaders and wisdom carriers, present in our governance and imagination as fully as in our intentions.

How the pieces relate

Wisdom listens. Stewardship protects. Integration weaves. Each council has its own legal vessel, and the charter of the Foundation binds it to serve the field the Wisdom Council holds.

Capital enters through the Living Treasury. Land and long-horizon assets enter the Living Trust. The Integration Council finds where a place is ready, and resources flow there through the Planetary Party Protocol and Flow Funding, with every flow traceable on the Living Ledger.

Edition One

The Living Constitution of Naluʻea

A living agreement for the flourishing of life across generations.

You hold these pages for only a little while. They were entrusted to you by those who came before. They do not belong to you. Nor did they belong to those who first wrote them. Their purpose is to help life flourish. Receive them with humility. Steward them with courage. Leave them wiser than you found them. Then place them gently into the hands of those who come after you.

This Constitution is a living document — Edition One, currently in active review and refinement with the First Steward Circle. What follows is the essence of what has come through. It will deepen as the circle gathers and as the Living System grows into its own understanding of itself.

I

Purpose

The purpose of Naluʻea is to steward the flourishing of life across generations.

It exists to cultivate the relationships through which people, communities, cultures, lands, waters, knowledge, governance, and capital may serve the continuity of life.

Every expression of Naluʻea shall remain faithful to this purpose. When uncertainty arises, this purpose shall guide interpretation. When circumstances change, this purpose shall remain.

II

Principles

These Principles of Stewardship form the constitutional heart of Naluʻea. They shall guide the interpretation of every Article, every structure, every relationship, and every decision undertaken in service of this Constitution.

ILife

Human flourishing cannot be separated from the flourishing of the greater living world. The wellbeing of people, waters, lands, forests, oceans, cultures, and all living beings arises through relationship, not separation. Whenever choices present competing interests, stewardship begins by asking what allows life itself to flourish most fully.

Life is the first beneficiary of every decision.

IIStewardship

Land, knowledge, wealth, institutions, and power are received in trust for a time. Every generation becomes a temporary steward of gifts it did not create and cannot rightfully possess forever. Stewardship asks not what may be controlled, but what must be cared for so that life may continue to flourish.

Nothing essential to life is ultimately owned.

IIIRelationship

Trust precedes coordination. Listening precedes action. Every enduring system arises from the quality of the relationships that give it life. Governance, capital, knowledge, and collaboration all derive their integrity from the relationships upon which they are built.

Relationship precedes transaction.

IVFuture Generations

Children, youth, and future generations are among those present at every table of stewardship. The future is already present in the children among us. Each generation receives the Earth in trust, with the responsibility to leave it more whole, more resilient, and more life-giving than it was found.

To steward well is to become a trustworthy ancestor.

III

Relationship

Relationship is the living fabric through which stewardship becomes possible. Every person, community, culture, institution, and living system exists within a greater web of relationships that gives rise to life itself.

Listening

Listening is the first practice of stewardship. Wisdom emerges through attentive relationship with people, place, and the living world. Through listening together, deeper understanding becomes possible.

Reciprocity

Every healthy relationship contains both giving and receiving. Communities flourish through mutual care. Knowledge grows through sharing. Resources circulate through generosity and responsibility.

Belonging

Life flourishes through the unique gifts of every person, community, culture, generation, and way of knowing. Wholeness arises as every unique expression finds its place in service to life.

IV

The Stewards

A Steward is one who willingly accepts temporary responsibility for the flourishing of life. Stewards receive this Constitution in trust and carry it faithfully for a time, knowing that every generation contributes to a story far greater than its own.

Stewardship is expressed through service, relationship, wisdom, courage, humility, and love.

Every Steward commits to embody the Purpose and Principles of this Constitution. To listen deeply. To protect the integrity of the living system while welcoming its continued evolution. To serve with humility, transparency, and accountability. To hold children, youth, and future generations among those present in every act of stewardship.

Every Steward receives life as an inheritance. Every Steward enriches that inheritance through faithful care. Every Steward entrusts it to those who follow.

V

The Living System

Life flourishes through living systems. Stewardship unfolds through relationships that remain responsive, interconnected, and continually learning.

The Naluʻea Living System continually expresses itself through essential functions of stewardship: listening, constitutional stewardship, coordination, learning, resource stewardship, community stewardship, and any future expressions called forth in faithful service to life.

A society devoted to stewardship cultivates the flourishing of every human being in right relationship with all life.

VI

The Formation of a Steward

Every Steward is first received. Every person enters life carrying inherent dignity, unique gifts, and a purpose that unfolds through relationship. As people flourish, they strengthen the flourishing of their communities, the living world, and future generations.

Receiving

Every life is welcomed with belonging. Communities cultivate environments where every person grows through love, safety, dignity, curiosity, joy, and meaningful contribution.

Discovering

Every person carries gifts waiting to unfold. Purpose reveals itself where unique gifts meet the needs of life.

Belonging

Communities cultivate Stewards. Stewards cultivate communities. Together they create the relationships through which life continually flourishes.

Responsibility

Each person learns to care for themselves. Families care for one another. Communities care for place. Humanity cares for the living world. Every widening circle strengthens the whole.

Naluʻea · A Living System of Stewardship · 2026

An invitation for capital to participate

How would you like your resources to participate in the flourishing of life?

Rather than asking you to fit a predefined financial product, Naluʻea begins with a different question: what promise accompanies this resource?

First, the promise your capital carries

Every contribution first enters the Living Treasury, which remembers the promise accompanying each resource. From the outside you experience one Treasury; inside, each kind of capital is tracked and honored through its own accounting.

Gift Capital

“I freely entrust this resource to serve life.”

Philanthropic gifts, foundation grants, donations, family and corporate philanthropy, bequests and legacy giving, plus community and crowdfunding participation at any scale. The principal is permanently stewarded and its yield joins the living current.

US donors give through the Naluʻea Ministry; European and international donors through the Naluʻea Foundation.

Strengthens the perpetual endowment

Stewardship Capital

“Please return it when its work is complete.”

Patient capital, zero-interest loans, revolving catalytic capital, recoverable grants, program-related investments, development finance and climate facilities. As projects mature, the principal returns home, ready for the next place that is ready.

Perpetual circulation

Investment Capital

“Regeneration and responsible financial return.”

Family offices, institutional investors, pension funds, insurers, sovereign wealth funds, mission-aligned investors and banks. Capital flows into regenerative enterprise, infrastructure and land stewardship; returns are shared as agreed while principal remains stewarded.

Shared yield

Legacy Capital

“These resources become part of life beyond my lifetime.”

Estates, land, businesses, intellectual property, family legacies and conservation easements. Some are permanently stewarded, some generate living yields, some strengthen community stewardship directly.

The intergenerational commons

Then, where your capital lands

Having found the kind of capital that fits, a second choice remains: at what level of the living system would you like your capital to land?

Proximity

A bioregion

Resource one living place: a watershed, community and circle of stewards you can see, visit and know by name, activated through the Planetary Party Protocol.

You plant a seed in one place.
Function

A domain

A dedicated stewardship pool for one field of impact across many places: sacred lands and waters, intergenerational learning, regenerative enterprise, cultural renewal and more.

One kind of growth, planted across many places.
Leverage

The planetary level

The team coordinates capital by need across the whole system, building what no single node can: verification and intelligence infrastructure, legal architecture and the perpetual endowment base.

You tend the watershed in which every seed can grow.
Wholeness

Community coherence

Fund community wellbeing as a primary outcome, verified through indicators the community itself defines rather than metrics imposed from outside.

Communities becoming more fully themselves.

How capital and assets flow

Whichever kind of capital and level you choose, every path joins the same current. This is not capital without accountability; it is capital whose accountability is alive rather than bureaucratic.

  1. Capital enters the Living Treasury

    Held in trust and invested according to a binding Investment Policy Statement.

  2. Readiness is cultivated

    Through the Planetary Party Protocol, a bioregion moves through sensing, seeing, flowing, celebrating and regenerating before resources arrive.

  3. Yield flows to ready places

    Through Flow Funding, resources reach trusted community stewards, deployed relationally and guided by lived knowledge of place rather than a funder’s predetermined criteria.

  4. Every flow is traceable

    The IXO Living Ledger records flows and impact credentials, verified by communities through indicators they define and transparent to all participants.

  5. Land enters the Living Trust

    Held outside the reach of any future board, market or crisis. What enters the Trust does not leave it.

  6. Value returns and circulates

    Yield returns to the Treasury, land regenerates, knowledge flows back through the network, and the next cycle of regeneration begins stronger.

Investment Policy Statement

The principles that govern the Treasury

The IPS is the written, binding discipline that makes the perpetual promise real. It is being finalized with qualified investment advisors and legal counsel. These five principles take precedence over return considerations wherever they conflict.

Request the full draft IPS

  • Stewardship before ownership

    Capital is held in guardianship for the flourishing of the whole, not the enrichment of any party.

  • Perpetuity

    The real, inflation-adjusted value of the principal is preserved so the endowment strengthens rather than depletes.

  • Mission alignment of the capital itself

    Assets are invested in service to life, not only deployed that way. The Treasury does not fund, through its holdings, what its mission exists to heal.

  • Relationship and sovereignty

    Where capital supports Living Nodes and communities, it respects their sovereignty and moves relationally.

  • Patient growth in cycles

    Capital is welcomed in step with the Roadmap; the architecture demonstrates stability before larger capital enters.

Crowdfunding to resource Living Nodes

Participation at every scale

A Liechtenstein crowdfunding license, activated through the Digital Innovation Hub, opens a new dimension of participation. Up to EUR 5 million per program per year can make each Living Node its own fundable entity.

The Liechtenstein Venture Cooperative gives any community, land project or regenerative enterprise an agile legal form, with impact reporting connected to the Living Ledger from the start. A family in Vermont can fund a node in Gabon; a pension fund in Germany can participate alongside a youth cooperative in South Africa.

A worked illustration

Valle Verde: four kinds of capital, one living place

Valle Verde is a hypothetical, composite community created as a teaching example. The patterns are real; the place is not. It is a 500-acre watershed in a mountainous Latin American bioregion, home to 80 families, at the headwaters of a river serving twelve downstream communities.

CapitalSourceAmountWhat it does
GiftFoundation grant and an individual donor$300,000Land into trust, compensation for twelve named stewards through the Mother Fund, cultural center Year 1
StewardshipCatalytic revolving fund$500,000Agroforestry expansion and cooperative infrastructure; principal returns by Year 5 for the next community
InvestmentMission-aligned family office$1,000,000Cacao cooperative scaling; principal preserved, a modest yield shared with the investor and the Treasury
LegacyA retiring land steward50 acresAdjacent forest placed in the Living Trust as intergenerational commons

Three years later, in the illustration

The watershed is permanently protected, twelve stewards are compensated for their tending, the cooperative produces export-grade cacao with net revenue shared among members, investor and Treasury, the catalytic capital is returning to serve the next community, and twelve downstream communities have cleaner, more reliable water.

Architecture for systemic transformation

The 12 Domains of Stewardship

Based on Barbara Marx Hubbard’s Wheel of Co-Creation, the 12 Domains are the backbone we use to map and organize ourselves. Every domain is both an area of crisis and an opportunity for regeneration. At the center sits worldview: when it flows from separation toward wholeness, the whole wheel turns with greater ease.

Inner ring:

Select any domain, Thread or Living Node to see how it connects. Hover over the wheel to trace links.

The Threads we’re weaving

Threads are the focused lines of work that run through the domains. Some align directly to a single domain. Others are more nuanced and span several, and in Bioregional Activation, communities choose their own combination of domains and expertise.

Roadmap

The pathway of formation, from founding seed to planetary scale

The Living Treasury grows in cycles, each a turn of a spiral returning to the whole system from a new vantage point. Capital moves when the system is genuinely ready, and sovereign-scale capital enters only after earlier cycles have demonstrated stability, governance maturity and verified regenerative returns.

What readiness means

Before capital moves between cycles, the Living System checks in with itself across six dimensions, held together: is what lies beneath our feet stable enough to carry what we are about to build?

People

The capacity, trust and timing of individuals and communities.

Technology

What is stable, what is still being built, and where the experiment is.

Resources

Money, people, materials and time, committed and accessible.

Learning capture

Storytellers, facilitators and documentation in place.

Governance

Agreements and decision-making structures ready to hold the work.

Financial transparency

Clear articulation of where resources go and what we hope to learn.

Milestones

The path so far, and what comes next

In the spirit of sensing before acting, we name what is established and what is still forming. Honesty is the foundation of every relationship this system seeks to build.

Each milestone marks a moment when intention became structure. The marker shows where we stand today; scroll sideways to follow the path in either direction.

The planetary tech stack

Information and capital don’t disappear into a black box

Stewardship requires trust, and trust requires transparency. Technology serves as enabling infrastructure, so communities, funders and partners can see how resources flow, what outcomes are emerging and how stewardship is practiced.

The layers are sequential: you can’t coordinate what you can’t see, you can’t verify what hasn’t been agreed, and you can’t finance what hasn’t been verified.

Explore IXO

More partners to come. These are the partners in place today. As the work grows, more will join the stack, each chosen for data sovereignty, interoperability and service to communities.

Impact verification with IXO

IXO, the Internet of Impacts, is a full-stack platform created in 2017 in Switzerland as a nonprofit open-source foundation and is ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified. Its Living Ledger lets communities define their own values and indicators, so stewardship becomes legible to capital without being captured by it.

Living-ledger and decentralized verification programs are active or deploying in South Africa through a UNICEF partnership, in Bioregional Impact Zones across Liechtenstein’s Alpine region, and across a 735,000-hectare landscape at Mayumba in Gabon.

Read more about IXO

Knowledge commons with Arcos Earth

Catalist Network’s Arcos Earth platform, built over four years, surfaces who is doing what and where, and lets knowledge compound across communities through a shared Global Commons. Its OMNI-Mapping process, a fiscally sponsored project of the Buckminster Fuller Institute, lays strategic and relational groundwork before any platform is chosen.

Catalist is steward-led: not founder-controlled, not investor-owned, not built for sale. Its Collaborative Operating Agreement, released under Creative Commons, separates ownership, governance and profit-sharing so mission prevails.

A note on AI

Artificial intelligence is a powerful tool for organizing and surfacing what is already known. It is not a substitute for the human and relational discernment needed at the genuine edge of what’s possible.

Every AI-assisted process in the stack preserves human agency and traceable provenance. No automated recommendation stands in for the lived judgment of the communities and stewards it serves. Technology serves life; it doesn’t decide on life’s behalf.

Back to Infrastructure

Planetary tech stack: verification and capital flow

IXO, the Internet of Impacts

Naluʻea doesn’t build verification infrastructure. It weaves the best tools already operating at scale into a coordination layer greater than any single technology. IXO is the primary verification partner in that stack.

What IXO is

A full-stack Spatial Web platform founded in 2017 in Switzerland as a nonprofit, open-source foundation. It is software for intelligent cooperation: it gives people, organizations, communities, devices and AI agents shared structure, rules and evidence to coordinate work, financing, verification and governance, while each keeps control of its own identity, data and decisions.

Its long-range vision is a global digital immune system for Earth and humanity: decentralized infrastructure for measuring, verifying and financing real-world impact at planetary scale. IXO runs its own Layer-1 blockchain, is ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified, and has been building for more than ten years, with live programs across Africa, Asia and Europe.

The Living Ledger

Rather than conventional measurement, reporting and verification imposed from outside, the Living Ledger is a continuous, governed record in which the community itself defines what value is.

  • Communities define their own cosmology and indicators, and the system holds them without imposing a single external framework.
  • Sacred site custodians, Indigenous knowledge holders and community forest stewards are included in how rewards flow.
  • Evidence from sensors, satellites, drones, bioacoustics, IoT devices and human verification comes together in one system.
  • Different cosmologies can sit on the platform and speak to one another; difference is made legible, not erased.

Each IXO Impact Credit carries its full provenance: the entity, claims, location, period, oracle, protocol, data and proof.

What IXO makes possible for Naluʻea

Digital twins for living places

A watershed, bioregion or land-stewardship relationship can have a verifiable digital presence, with its own identity, history and ability to participate in capital flows.

Verification of biocultural services

A path to what the founding circle named as an aim: rewarding the quality of people’s relationship with land, making ceremony, watershed tending and cultural continuity legible to capital without reducing them to it.

Bioregional Impact Zones

Each Living Node can become a digital twin of its bioregion, with its own Living Ledger, ventures, treasury and governance, and natural capital given verifiable weight alongside financial flows.

A community coherence credit

The teams are exploring a new class of impact verification that goes beyond carbon and biodiversity to honor systemic health, built on IXO’s full-provenance credit infrastructure.

Live proof points

IXO is operational, not theoretical. Its partners and funders have included UBS, UNICEF, Coinbase Giving, Gold Standard, South Pole, UC Berkeley, Temasek Foundation, the Interchain Foundation and sovereign governments across Africa, Asia and Europe.

  • UNICEF, South Africa

    A contracted program of about CHF 1 million deploying the Living Ledger with young people as human verification agents across 30 organizations, with the data held as a sovereign matter by South Africa’s Presidency.

  • Clean cooking, Africa

    A flagship implementation tracking clean cookstove projects in real time through decentralized digital verification, recognized by UC Berkeley’s Carbon Trading Project for high-quality carbon credits.

  • UBS and UNICEF, India

    A multi-year research and development collaboration on outcomes-based financing for educational technology.

  • Zambia and Article 6

    A Zambia–Sweden partnership under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, validating the infrastructure for sovereign-level carbon accounting.

  • PathGen, Singapore

    A pathogen genomics intelligence platform launched in December 2025 with Duke-NUS and hosted by Temasek Foundation.

The Liechtenstein bridge

The living connection between IXO and Naluʻea is Franz Allmayer: founder of Hypha, an IXO board member and holder of the Liechtenstein Digital Innovation Hub mandate. Trained as a biomedical engineer, he worked with WHO, the Gates Foundation and the Clinton Foundation before turning to the architecture of money itself, seeing value as something that should circulate like rivers through a landscape.

Through the Hub, supported by the European Commission and the Principality of Liechtenstein, Franz is deploying an IXO-based system for Liechtenstein and the Alpine bioregion, including cooperative enterprise digital twins, community currency systems and supply-chain transparency.

Planetary tech stack: sensemaking and knowledge commons

Arcos Earth

Across thousands of organizations and movements already doing the work, the knowledge, people, relationships and resources exist. What’s missing is the connective tissue that lets them see one another and act together. Arcos Earth, built by Catalist Network, is that connective tissue: deployed and running today.

Three layers, one source of truth

Arcos holds knowledge at three scales at once. At every scale, the people who hold the knowledge decide how far it travels, item by item, and can change that decision later.

  • Personal

    Each person has a library that belongs to them. An Elder’s recordings, stories and reflections live here first, and nothing leaves unless they choose to share it.

  • Community

    A family, a nation or a network gathers in its own space to organize, learn and make sense together. Each community sets its own guidelines, and event spaces gather focused knowledge for a particular occasion.

  • Global

    When a community chooses, what it has learned can be offered to others so no one starts over, and the community can speak for itself in its own voice. Nothing reaches this layer by default.

Knowledge stays whole

The architecture is relational. It preserves relationships, origin and significance instead of reducing knowledge to isolated data points. A traditional navigator was also an ethnobotanist, an astronomer and a healer; Arcos is built to hold knowledge that whole while still letting it be shared across silos.

Through OMNI-Mapping, a fiscally sponsored project of the Buckminster Fuller Institute, Arcos has mapped more than 200 sustainability, resilience and regeneration frameworks against one another while honoring their distinctions, so Indigenous knowledge, ecological data, science and community wisdom can inform each other without being flattened.

Why it matters now

Naluʻea’s near-term readiness rests on one move: making visible, likely for the first time, how large this movement already is. An early, low-cost deployment of Arcos mapping and commons infrastructure surfaces and connects aligned communities and practitioners, producing immediate, measurable evidence of the coherence the Treasury is built to compound.

Funding here builds the first ecosystem map and knowledge commons across the Naluʻea constellation, the tools that let nodes and stewards find each other, and the runway for the small steward core that holds it. It de-risks everything downstream: verification and coordination are far more valuable once the field they serve can be seen.

How Arcos is held

Catalist is steward-led: not founder-controlled, not investor-owned and not built for sale. Its Collaborative Operating Agreement, released under Creative Commons, binds the mission into how the company is built. Catalist cannot own the data, investors cannot own the company, and there is no exit. Capital participates through a flat, capped return without capturing the system, the same posture Naluʻea holds.

What its written policy guarantees each community

  • The knowledge is the community’s

    It can be exported in full at any time, and nothing is deleted without a written request.

  • Ending a relationship exposes nothing

    Visibility settings carry over unchanged, and archived spaces are private by default.

  • No featuring without permission

    Any public or marketing use needs written opt-in, which can be revoked. Silence is not consent.

  • No judging of cultural content

    Catalist does not judge the accuracy or cultural sensitivity of what a community holds.

  • Continuity of care

    After a subscription ends, the space stays viewable at no charge for 12 months, with full export rights for named stewards.

Proof in practice

The Mashantucket Pequot Tribal Nation is using Arcos, at its own expense, to build an inter-tribal relationship map that shows tribal people to one another and strengthens connections between nations, land and water. Elders guide and connect while younger members do the hands-on entry, and the work grows outward from one anchor community. Their requirements, including people controlling their own information and nothing becoming public unless explicitly shared, are shaping how the platform protects knowledge.

Catalist also helped shape requirements for community knowledge governance in Pyxera Global’s Partnership 4 Digital Justice, contributing principles such as sovereignty as the starting position, per-item consent, and consent that people can actually read and understand.
